stimulus: A seismologist's field station records ground motion during an aftershock sequence. When recording begins, the station's data buffer has 1,200 megabytes of free space. While the sequence continues, the station fills 45 megabytes of the buffer every 3 minutes. Let $F$ be the free space, in megabytes, left in the buffer $t$ minutes after recording begins.
explanation: The free space at $t = 0$ is 1,200 megabytes, so that is the constant term. The buffer fills 45 megabytes every 3 minutes, which is $45 \div 3 = 15$ megabytes per minute. Free space is going down, so the rate is negative. That gives $F = 1{,}200 - 15t$.

A.why: You used the 45 megabytes as if it were filled every minute. That amount is filled every 3 minutes, so you need to divide by 3 to get the rate per minute.

C.why: You gave the slope the wrong sign. Recording uses up free space, so $F$ goes down as $t$ goes up and the rate must be negative.

D.why: You swapped the starting amount and the rate. The 1,200 megabytes is the value when $t = 0$, so it is the constant, and 15 is the change per minute, so it multiplies $t$.

stem: Which equation represents this relationship for $w \geq 2$?
stimulus: A marine biologist monitors a coral colony during a marine heat wave. When the heat stress begins, the colony has 340 square centimeters of living tissue. For the first 2 weeks it loses no tissue. After that, it loses 18 square centimeters of living tissue every 3 weeks. Let $A$ be the area of living tissue, in square centimeters, $w$ weeks after the heat stress begins.
explanation: The tissue loss is $18 \div 3 = 6$ square centimeters per week, and it only starts after week 2. The number of weeks with loss is $w - 2$, so $A = 340 - 6(w - 2)$. Check: at $w = 2$ this gives 340, which is correct because nothing has been lost yet.

A.why: You applied the loss from week 0. The first 2 weeks have no loss, so only $w - 2$ weeks count.

B.why: You used 18 as a weekly rate. The colony loses 18 square centimeters every 3 weeks, so the weekly rate is 6.

C.why: You shifted the input the wrong way. Adding 2 counts 2 extra weeks of loss. The loss-free weeks have to be subtracted, which gives $w - 2$.

stimulus: A nutrition science study gives each participant a daily target of 2,000 calories. One participant eats a 450-calorie breakfast. For the rest of the day, the participant eats only snacks, and each snack is 2 servings of a yogurt with 80 calories per serving. Let $R$ be the number of calories left under the daily target after the breakfast and $n$ snacks.
explanation: After breakfast, $2{,}000 - 450 = 1{,}550$ calories are left, and that is the starting value. Each snack is 2 servings of 80 calories, so it uses $2 \times 80 = 160$ calories. The remaining amount goes down with each snack, so $R = 1{,}550 - 160n$.

B.why: You used the calories in one serving. Each snack has 2 servings, so each snack uses 160 calories, not 80.

C.why: You started from the full target and left out the breakfast. When $n = 0$, only 1,550 calories remain.

D.why: You added the snack calories. Eating uses up the remaining allowance, so the slope has to be negative.

stimulus: An ecology group is restoring a burned hillside. Before the current project begins, 120 native saplings have already been planted there. On each day of the project, 4 volunteer crews each plant 25 more saplings. Let $N$ be the total number of saplings planted on the hillside after $d$ days of the project.
explanation: The 120 saplings already in the ground are the value when $d = 0$. Each day, 4 crews plant 25 saplings each, which is $4 \times 25 = 100$ saplings per day. So $N = 120 + 100d$.

A.why: You counted only one crew. There are 4 crews planting 25 each, so the daily rate is 100.

B.why: You swapped the starting amount and the rate. The 120 saplings were there at the start, so 120 is the constant, and the 100 planted each day multiplies $d$.

D.why: You added the number of crews to the saplings per crew. The daily total is 4 crews times 25 saplings, which is 100.

stimulus: A civil engineering firm is boring a road tunnel that will be 2,400 meters long when complete. So far, the boring machine has dug 600 meters of the tunnel. From now on, it will advance 18 meters per day. Let $L$ be the length of tunnel, in meters, that still has to be dug $d$ days from now.
explanation: Right now, $2{,}400 - 600 = 1{,}800$ meters are still left to dig, so that is the value when $d = 0$. Each day removes 18 meters from what is left, so the rate is $-18$. That gives $L = 1{,}800 - 18d$.

A.why: You started from the full tunnel length and ignored the 600 meters already dug. When $d = 0$, only 1,800 meters are left.

C.why: This equation gives the length already dug. The question asks for the length still left to dig.

D.why: You gave the slope the wrong sign. The length left to dig gets shorter every day, so the rate must be negative.

stem: Which equation represents this relationship for $T \geq 20$?
stimulus: In a materials science lab, a metal alloy rod is 250 centimeters long at a temperature of 20 degrees Celsius ($^\circ\text{C}$). As it is heated above $20^\circ\text{C}$, its length increases by 0.03 centimeter for every $10^\circ\text{C}$ rise in temperature. Let $L$ be the length of the rod, in centimeters, at a temperature of $T$ degrees Celsius.
explanation: The rod grows $0.03 \div 10 = 0.003$ centimeter per degree. The growth is measured from $20^\circ\text{C}$, so the number of degrees of heating is $T - 20$. That gives $L = 250 + 0.003(T - 20)$. Check: at $T = 20$ the length is 250, as stated.

B.why: You measured the temperature rise from $0^\circ\text{C}$. The rod is 250 centimeters at $20^\circ\text{C}$, so the rise is $T - 20$. Your equation gives a length above 250 at $20^\circ\text{C}$.

C.why: You used 0.03 as the change per degree. That change happens every $10^\circ\text{C}$, so you need to divide by 10.

D.why: You shifted the input the wrong way. Adding 20 counts 20 degrees of heating that never happened. The degrees of heating are $T - 20$.

rated_why: Multi-step: convert rate per 10°C to per 1°C, handle offset from reference temperature (T-20), and defend against 0.03T and other distractors

stimulus: A labour economist is studying a union contract. The contract sets a starting wage of \$19.40 per hour. It also gives a raise of \$0.35 per hour twice every year, once in January and once in July. Let $W$ be the hourly wage, in dollars, of a worker who has been under the contract for $t$ full years.
explanation: The starting wage of \$19.40 is the value when $t = 0$. There are two raises of \$0.35 each year, which adds $2 \times 0.35 = 0.70$ dollars per hour per year. So $W = 19.40 + 0.70t$.

A.why: You counted only one raise per year. The contract gives two raises each year, so the yearly increase is \$0.70.

B.why: You swapped the starting value and the rate. The \$19.40 is the wage at the start, so it is the constant, and the yearly increase multiplies $t$.

C.why: You divided by 2 when you should have multiplied. There are 2 raises each year, so they add up to more than \$0.35 a year, not less.

stimulus: An ornithologist tracks a GPS-tagged snow goose at the end of its migration. When tracking starts, the goose is flying at an altitude of 3,200 meters. From then on, it drops 150 meters every 2 minutes as it glides toward a wetland. Let $H$ be the goose's altitude, in meters, $t$ minutes after tracking starts.
explanation: The altitude at $t = 0$ is 3,200 meters. The goose drops 150 meters every 2 minutes, which is $150 \div 2 = 75$ meters per minute. It is losing altitude, so the rate is negative. That gives $H = 3{,}200 - 75t$.

A.why: You used 150 meters as a drop per minute. That drop takes 2 minutes, so you need to divide by 2.

B.why: You multiplied by 2 instead of dividing. A drop of 150 meters over 2 minutes is 75 meters per minute, not 300.

D.why: You gave the slope the wrong sign. The goose is descending, so its altitude goes down over time and the rate must be negative.

stem: Which equation represents this situation, where $n$ is the number of sea stars counted on the first survey?
stimulus: A marine biologist surveyed sea stars along the same stretch of rocky shoreline twice. The number counted on the second survey was 8 fewer than 3 times the number counted on the first survey. The two surveys together counted 92 sea stars.
explanation: The second survey is "8 fewer than 3 times" $n$, so you triple $n$ first and then subtract 8, which gives $3n - 8$. The total is the first survey plus the second survey: $n + (3n - 8) = 92$. As a check, $n = 25$ gives $25 + 67 = 92$.

A.why: You subtracted 8 from $n$ before tripling, which gives 3 times (8 fewer than $n$). The text says 8 fewer than 3 times $n$, so the subtraction comes after the multiplication.

B.why: You set the second survey alone equal to 92. The 92 is the total for both surveys, so you also have to add the first survey's $n$.

D.why: You reversed the subtraction. "8 fewer than $3n$" means $3n - 8$, not $8 - 3n$.

stem: Which equation represents this situation, where $w$ is the width, in inches, of the panel?
stimulus: A folklorist is building a rectangular exhibit panel to display illustrated cards of regional trickster tales. The length of the panel is 5 inches longer than twice its width. A decorative strip will run once around the entire edge of the panel, and the strip needs to be 118 inches long.
explanation: The length is 5 more than twice the width, which is $2w + 5$. A strip around the entire edge is the perimeter: two widths plus two lengths. That gives $2w + 2(2w + 5) = 118$. As a check, $w = 18$ gives a length of 41, and $2(18) + 2(41) = 118$.

A.why: You added one width and one length. That is only half of the perimeter, and the strip runs around all four sides.

C.why: You multiplied width by length, which gives the area. The strip's length depends on the perimeter, not the area.

D.why: You mixed up the two numbers and wrote the length as 5 times the width plus 2. "5 longer than twice the width" means $2w + 5$.

stem: Which expression represents the total cost, in dollars, of the order, where $n$ is the number of ceramic specimens ordered?
stimulus: A materials science lab is ordering test specimens for a fracture-toughness study. Each ceramic specimen costs $18. Each alloy specimen costs $7 more than a ceramic specimen. The lab orders 3 times as many alloy specimens as ceramic specimens.
explanation: Each alloy specimen costs $18 + 7 = 25$ dollars, and the lab orders $3n$ of them. The ceramic specimens cost $18n$ and the alloy specimens cost $25(3n)$, so the total is $18n + 25(3n)$.

A.why: You used the $7 difference as the price of an alloy specimen. Each one costs $7 more than $18, which is $25.

B.why: You found the correct alloy price but left out the fact that there are 3 times as many alloy specimens. This expression prices only $n$ of them.

stem: Which equation represents this situation, where $d$ is the number of aftershocks recorded on the first day?
stimulus: A seismologist tracked the aftershocks that followed a moderate earthquake. The number recorded on the second day was 12 fewer than the number recorded on the first day. The number recorded on the third day was half the number recorded on the second day. Over the three days, the station recorded 132 aftershocks.
explanation: The second day is $d - 12$. The third day is half of the second day's count, so you halve the whole expression: $\frac{d - 12}{2}$. Adding the three days gives $d + (d - 12) + \frac{d - 12}{2} = 132$. As a check, $d = 60$ gives $60 + 48 + 24 = 132$.

B.why: You doubled the second day's count instead of halving it. The third day had half as many aftershocks as the second day, not twice as many.

C.why: You halved only $d$ and then subtracted 12. The third day is half of the entire second-day count $d - 12$, so the 12 has to be halved too.

D.why: You reversed the subtraction. "12 fewer than $d$" means $d - 12$, not $12 - d$.

rated_why: Two-step with subtle trap: day 3 requires recognizing that 'half the second day' means (d−12)/2, not d/2−12.

stem: Which equation represents this situation, where $b$ is the number of B cells per microliter in the sample?
stimulus: An immunologist counted three types of lymphocytes in one microliter of a blood sample. The number of T cells was 4 times the number of B cells. The number of natural killer cells was 150 more than the number of B cells. Altogether, the three types numbered 2,550 cells per microliter.
explanation: The T cells are $4b$ and the natural killer cells are $b + 150$. The total adds all three types: $b + 4b + (b + 150) = 2{,}550$. As a check, $b = 400$ gives $400 + 1{,}600 + 550 = 2{,}550$.

A.why: You read "150 more than" as "150 times." "More than" means you add 150 to $b$, not multiply $b$ by 150.

C.why: You added the T cells and the natural killer cells but left out the B cells. The total includes all three types.

D.why: You used 150 as the natural killer count. 150 is how many more natural killer cells there are than B cells, so the count is $b + 150$.

stem: Which equation represents this situation, where $p$ is the number of Baroque pieces on the program?
stimulus: A musicologist is planning a recital program. Each Baroque piece on the program lasts 6 minutes. Each Romantic piece lasts 9 minutes. There are 2 more Romantic pieces than Baroque pieces. The program also includes one 15-minute intermission, and the whole program lasts 123 minutes.
explanation: There are $p + 2$ Romantic pieces, and each lasts 9 minutes, so they take $9(p + 2)$ minutes. Add the Baroque time $6p$ and the 15-minute intermission: $6p + 9(p + 2) + 15 = 123$. As a check, $p = 6$ gives $36 + 72 + 15 = 123$.

A.why: You didn't put parentheses around $p + 2$, so the 9 minutes multiplied only $p$. Each of the 2 extra Romantic pieces also lasts 9 minutes.

B.why: You read "2 more than" as "2 times." The number of Romantic pieces is $p + 2$, not $2p$.

D.why: You left out the 15-minute intermission. The 123 minutes covers the whole program, including the intermission.

stem: Which equation represents this situation, where $L$ is the length, in inches, of the coverlet?
stimulus: A textile historian is making a reproduction of a nineteenth-century woven coverlet. The coverlet is rectangular, and its width is 18 inches less than its length. Fringe will be sewn along both long sides and along the bottom edge only. The top edge gets no fringe. The fringe needed totals 246 inches.
explanation: The width is $L - 18$. The fringe covers two lengths, $2L$, and one width, $L - 18$. So the equation is $2L + (L - 18) = 246$. As a check, $L = 88$ gives $176 + 70 = 246$.

B.why: You used the full perimeter. The top edge gets no fringe, so only one width is included.

C.why: You doubled the width and counted the length once. The fringe runs along both long sides, so the length is the dimension that gets counted twice.

D.why: You reversed the subtraction. "18 inches less than the length" means $L - 18$, not $18 - L$.

rated_why: Requires spatial reasoning (which dimension is which, which sides get fringe); the explicit constraint helps, but geometry adds a step beyond pure algebra.

stem: Which expression represents the number of cycad fossils on the slab in terms of $c$?
stimulus: A paleobotanist is cataloging plant fossils preserved in a single shale slab, which contains $c$ conifer fossils. The number of fern fossils on the slab is 7 less than twice the number of conifer fossils. The number of cycad fossils is one-third the number of fern fossils.
explanation: The fern count is 7 less than twice $c$, which is $2c - 7$. The cycad count is one-third of that whole fern count, so you divide the entire expression by 3: $\frac{2c - 7}{3}$. As a check, $c = 20$ gives 33 ferns and 11 cycads.

A.why: You divided only the $2c$ by 3 and then subtracted 7. One-third applies to the whole fern count, so the 7 has to be divided by 3 as well.

B.why: You multiplied the fern count by 3. The cycad count is one-third of the fern count, not three times it.

C.why: You reversed the subtraction. "7 less than twice $c$" means $2c - 7$, not $7 - 2c$.
